ORDER None for the respondent No.1
inspite of service of notice.

respondent No.2 has not been served.
2. Heard on I.A. No.14686/2024 - an application under Section 5 of the Limitation Act for conodation of delay.
As per office note, appeal is barred by 106 days.

For the reasons stated in the application which is duly supported by affidavit of appellant, I.A. No.14686/2024 is allowed and the delay in presentation of the appeal is hereby condoned.
3 . Also heard on the question of admission.
The appeal is admitted for hearing.
With consent of learned counsel for the parties, the matter is heard finally and is disposed of accordingly.

4. This miscellaneous appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988 has been filed by the claimant being aggrieved of award dated 08.01.2024 passed by the learned Member, IIIrd Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Katni (for short the "Claims Tribunal") in Motor Accident Claim NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:6632 2 MA-5787-2024 Case No.916/2021 (Jagdish Prasad Choudhary Vs. Akash Choudhary & Others) for enhancement of compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal.

sentences.text: On account of the accident, which took place on 16.11.2020 with an auto bearing registration No.MP-21-R-5154 causing multiple injuries to the claimant, the learned Claims Tribunal after recording a finding of 21% disability of whole body and 35% permanent disability in the injured part has awarded a compensation of Rs.3,63,197/- alongwith interest @ 6% per annum.
6. In the present appeal, appellant/claimant has sought enhancement of Rs.2,00,000/-, for which court fees of Rs.5,000/- has already been paid.
7. The submission of learned counsel for the appellant is that there was disability to the extent of 21% for the whole body and on the injured part, there was permanent disability of 35%.

It is further submitted that income of the injured/claimant has been taken by the Claims Tribunal as Rs.7,000/-
per month whereas on the date of accident i.e. on 16.11.2020, as per the applicable minimum wages in the State of M.P., it should have been taken as Rs.8,400/-.
Thus, it is prayed that the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal be enhanced.
8. Learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has supported the impugned award and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

9. On perusal of the record, this Court is of the view that looking to the disability sustained by the claimant, the compensation awarded by the Claims Tribunal is on lower side and the correct calculation for compensation would be as follows:-

sentences.text: Hence, the amount of compensation, to which the appellant/claimant would be entitled to, is Rs.5,85,317/-.
The Tribunal has already awarded sum of Rs.3,63,197/-.

Hence, the compensation enhanced by Rs.2,20,120/- (Rs.5,85,317/- - Rs.3,63,197/-), which is restricted to Rs.2,00,000/-
(Rupees Two Lakhs) as appeal is valued at Rs.2,00,000/- and Court Fee of Rs.5,000/- has been paid.
The other terms and conditions of the impugned award passed by the learned Claims Tribunal including rate of interest shall remain intact.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-JBP:6632 4 MA-5787-2024 11.

It is informed that in the Pre-sitting of Lok-Adalat, the case was settled between the parties for a sum of Rs.1,80,000/- as compensation to the claimant and docket for the same was signed by learned counsel for both the parties; but, the concerned authority/officer of the Oriental Insurance Company did not sign the docket and consequently, matter could not be disposed of in Lok-Adalat which causes loss of Rs.20,000/- to the Insurance Company.
12
Let the Insurance Company pay the enhanced amount along with interest as determined by the Tribunal.

So far as the loss of Rs.20,000/- caused to the Insurance Company is concerned, the Managing Director of Oriental Insurance Company Ltd. is free to recover the aforesaid excess amount of Rs.20,000/- from the delinquent officer of the Insurance Company who did not sign the docket.

13. Let a copy of this order be sent to the Managing Director, Oriental Insurance Company Limited,
Mumbai.
14.
Let the record of Tribunal be sent to the concerned Tribunal.
15. In above terms, this misc. appeal is disposed of.

(AVANINDRA KUMAR SINGH) JUDGE @shish Jagdish Prasad Choudhary vs Akash Choudhary on 6 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/8099619/
